notesDetails.title: Retroactive Git History vs. Actual Workflow
bullets: What was requested: PROMPT.md and AGENTS.md asked the agent to work through PLAN.md one slice at a time (S0–S7), adding one failing test at a time, marking [x], and committing after each task.
The agent spent the first 22.5 minutes (lines 1–301, 150 LLM calls) building and debugging the entire codebase with zero git commits.

It frequently wrote full implementations before tests—for example, writing all 219 lines of request.ex (line 51) before request_test.exs (line 53), and writing runner.ex (line 79) before runner_test.exs (line 85).

In the final 4 minutes (lines 311–325), it ran Python scripts to uncheck and re-check PLAN.md slice-by-slice and create 8 sequential commits. Because all of lib/ was already committed in S1 (35084a9), the final 3 commits (S5–S7) only touched PLAN.md.

notesDetails.title: Two Subtle Systems Bugs Consumed ~40% of the Run
bullets: Out of 32 failed tool results (isError: true), almost all stemmed from two subtle OS/BEAM interactions:

1. A FIFO Deadlock in :file_server_2 Disguised as a TLS Bug (Lines 97, 151–203, 245–251): Because the BEAM intercepts SIGINT for its BREAK menu, the agent created a wrapper script cb that created a named pipe (mkfifo) via CB_INTERRUPT_FIFO and spawned a watcher in cli.ex calling File.read(fifo) (line 97). In Erlang/OTP, File.read/1 routes through :file_server_2, and opening a FIFO with no writer blocked the entire BEAM file server. When testing HTTPS with CB_CA_CERT_FILE via ./cb (lines 154–190, 10 consecutive failing test runs), File.read!(ca_file) inside request.ex hung waiting on :file_server_2, causing every CLI HTTPS request to time out after 6s even though direct CapyBench.Request.get/1 calls succeeded. At line 193, the agent replaced File.read(fifo) with Port.open spawning /bin/cat <fifo>, fixing TLS—only to discover at line 245 (ps -ef) that every non-interrupted run leaked an orphaned /bin/cat process, requiring another round of wrapper cleanup (lines 247–251).

2. Sandbox PTY Restrictions on Ctrl-C Testing (Lines 39–40, 145, 223–237): Python's pty.openpty() failed with PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted inside the sandbox (lines 40 & 145). The agent bypassed this at line 223 by using macOS /usr/bin/script -q /dev/null ./cb ... to allocate a pseudo-TTY and send \x03.
3. Edit Tool Mismatches (6 errors): 6 of the 32 tool errors were edit calls failing due to non-unique or mismatched oldText (lines 120, 198, 210, 270, 282, 294).

notesDetails.title: Prompt Caching Saved 85% of the Run Cost ($9.97 Saved)
bullets: 98.28% Cache Hit Rate: Out of 5,632,768 total input tokens across 160 turns, 5,536,000 were served from cache (cacheRead) with zero cache invalidations/drops as the context grew steadily from 1,753 tokens (turn 1) to 74,400 tokens (turn 160).
Implied Unit Pricing & Savings: Uncached Input: $2.00 / 1M tokens • Cached Input (cacheRead): $0.20 / 1M tokens (90% discount) • Output: $10.00 / 1M tokens.
Without prefix caching, this run would have cost $11.69 instead of $1.72.

notesDetails.title: Latency Split, Tool Batching, and Reasoning Profile
bullets: 50/50 LLM vs. Tool Wall-Clock Split: Total wall-clock time: 26m 59s (1,619.3s). LLM inference time: 13m 41s (820.5s, 50.7%), averaging 5.13s/turn (min 1.10s, max 25.52s when writing request.ex). Tool execution time: 13m 19s (798.8s, 49.3%), dominated by repeated mix escript.build and mix test runs containing multi-second benchmark/timeout sleeps.
Almost Zero Tool Parallelism: Out of 159 toolUse turns, 157 turns called only a single tool (only the first 2 exploration turns batched 4 tool calls).

Selective Reasoning despite thinkingLevel: "high": Reasoning tokens averaged just 98.7 tokens/turn (15,787 total, 37.6% of output tokens). 46 of 160 turns (28.8%) used 0 reasoning tokens (primarily firing mix format && mix test immediately after an edit), while complex debugging/verification turns spiked up to 1,258 reasoning tokens (line 287).
